entries.title: Long articles get a glossary that covers them
entries.body: The Glossary now asks for a number of terms that grows with the length of the piece, up to 80 at a time where it used to ask for at most 20, and Find more asks for as many as the article's length still calls for. It is also asked to include people, places, works and events the piece names without introducing them, even when it mentions them only once, in passing, and to cover every part of a long article or a book rather than only the start.

entries.title: The article is set in a narrower column
entries.body: Lines of the article are shorter: the text column is 56 character-widths across where it was 65, and quotations and boxed notes are 7 character-widths narrower than that. Shorter lines are easier for the eye to follow from the end of one to the start of the next.

entries.title: The part on screen stands out more
entries.body: In the strip showing where you are in the article, the stretch on screen stays at full strength and the rest is dimmed, replacing the orange wash. The strip also ends above the bar at the bottom of the window, so the end of the article is no longer hidden behind it.

entries.title: Bigger buttons when you tap a paragraph
entries.body: On a phone or tablet, the row of buttons that appears when you tap a paragraph has larger buttons, at least 40 pixels in each direction, with no gaps between them. They are easier to hit with a finger; the row covers a little more of the paragraph above it.

entries.title: Summary's Thread is written when you open it
entries.body: Ticking 'Generate the main modes as soon as it opens' when you add an article no longer prepares Summary's Thread. It is written the first time you open it instead, so nothing is spent on a thread nobody reads.

entries.title: More space between paragraphs in AI answers
entries.body: Answers in Chat, the AI's replies to your comments, and answers to questions asked on the Help page leave more space between one paragraph and the next. A long answer is easier to take in a paragraph at a time.

entries.title: Try again appears after a failed dictation
entries.body: When dictation failed in a way that could be retried, Try again was missing if rough words had already appeared in the box, as they do in Chrome and browsers built on it. It appears now. A retry replaces the rough words when it can find them unchanged; otherwise it adds the text at your cursor, keeping your edits.

entries.title: Footnote marks no longer push lines apart
entries.body: A footnote mark, or any small raised or lowered text, could make its line sit further from the lines around it, so the spacing of the article looked uneven. Lines keep an even spacing whatever marks they carry.
